Region Midtjylland is one of the five Danish administrative regions and a key participant in the [[dansk-kvalitetsdatabase-for-inflammatoriske-tarmsygdomme|Dansk Kvalitetsdatabase for Inflammatoriske Tarmsygdomme]] (DANIBD). The region plays a significant role in the national effort to systematize and improve the treatment of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) in Denmark. It contributes both nursing and chief physician expertise to the DANIBD steering committee, alongside providing extensive clinical data, underscoring its interdisciplinary commitment to healthcare quality improvement [^src1].

In terms of patient demographics and diagnostics, Region Midtjylland handles a substantial portion of the national IBD patient burden. Between October 1, 2022, and September 30, 2023, the region registered 7,520 IBD patients, making it one of the most active regions alongside [[region-hovedstaden|Region Hovedstaden]] and [[region-syddanmark|Region Syddanmark]] [^src1]. Within this cohort, [[dk50-crohns-sygdom|DK50* Crohns sygdom]] accounted for 43% of all IBD patients in the region, while [[dk51-ulceroes-colitis|DK51* Ulcerøs colitis]] represented 56% [^src1]. Additionally, the region recorded 55 cases of [[dk830f-primaer-skleroserende-kolangitis|DK830F Primær skleroserende kolangitis]], a severe comorbid condition [^src1].

Beyond data contribution, Region Midtjylland actively engages in the evaluation and critique of national quality indicators, as seen in its formal feedback to the [[danibd-aarsrapport-2024]] [^src4]. The region has provided constructive criticism regarding specific quality metrics. For instance, Aarhus Universitetshospital (located in the region) argued that Indicator 1 does not accurately reflect the quality of diagnostic workups, noting that some patients had sufficient investigations at other hospitals or declined colonoscopies [^src4]. Furthermore, Regionshospitalet Gødstrup conducted a journal audit on Indicator 6 (re-operations) and concluded that the re-operation rate is a poor measure of surgical quality in IBD, suggesting anastomotic leakage as a better metric, similar to cancer surgery standards [^src4].
